P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, for exporters. Bank of Lao PDR Decision No. 333/BOL on export income in foreign currency took effect on 29 March 2024. It covers exports of goods and services. Exporters must receive foreign payments by bank transfer into a dedicated import-export account within the contract timeline, and no later than 180 days after export. Minimum shares of that income must be brought into Laos and sold to Lao commercial banks; the ratios vary and can change. How this applies to individual freelancers was not confirmed.
P1_fx_receipts.note: Single secondary source (Tilleke & Gibbins) captured on 2026-10-22; BOL decision text not captured.

sources.quote: 333 sets minimum required proportions for importing income in foreign currency derived from the exportation of goods and services, as well as the timeframe for doing so.

sources.title: Laos Regulates Management of Foreign Currency from Exports
sources.quote: Importing Foreign-Currency Income Exporters must receive payments from abroad via bank transfer into a dedicated bank account designated for import-export business activities within the timeline specified in the sale-purchase agreement, but not exceeding 180 days from the date of export.

P1_fx_receipts.notes: TRAP: services exports are in scope of Decision 333 (title covers goods and services).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. BCEL, the largest state commercial bank, publishes savings and fixed-deposit rates for individuals in USD and THB as well as kip (e.g. a USD savings account for individuals at 1.15% a year in the captured rate sheet). Foreign-currency availability for withdrawals and conversion has been tight at times (search summary), so do not count on getting cash dollars quickly.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Enterprises, including individual enterprises (sole proprietorships), register with the Ministry of Industry and Commerce's enterprise registration department. Since 15 October 2018 the enterprise registration certificate carries the tax identification number. The enterprise must then complete its tax information with the tax administration within 90 days of getting the licence. Fees and the rules for unregistered individual freelancers were not captured.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Registered enterprises receive their TIN on the enterprise registration certificate. Taxpayers without an enterprise (individuals, organisations) obtain a TIN from the tax office, and can apply themselves via the tax service portal (taxservice.mof.gov.la) in the provinces and districts covered.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Income Tax Law No. 67/NA (18 June 2019) applies tax on a worldwide basis. Residents for individual income tax are those permanently residing, living, earning a living or doing business in Laos. Individuals with annual income of LAK 50,000,001–400,000,000 pay a turnover-based rate: 1% for production, 2% for trade and 3% for services. Larger businesses pay profit tax at progressive rates of 0–20%.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 10%. Exports of goods are zero-rated (except unfinished natural resources), but the VAT Law has no concept of export services: PwC reads all services, including services exported by VAT-registered businesses, as subject to 10%. Registered enterprises are automatically in the VAT system unless they are micro enterprises. A LAK 400m registration threshold is reported in guides but was not captured. Deloitte 2026 confirms the 10% rate and that everyone except micro enterprises must register.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Law on Electronic Data Protection No. 25/NA (12 May 2017) applies, with an Implementation Instruction of 8 August 2018 and the Law on Electronic Transactions (2022). It classifies electronic data: collecting, using or disclosing sensitive data needs the data subject's consent, and so does transferring data collected in Laos abroad. There is no comprehensive controller/processor regime.

sources.title: Multilaw Data Protection Laws Guide — Laos (Tilleke & Gibbins Lao)

L5_data_protection.notes: TRAP: consent needed for cross-border transfer — relevant when using foreign SaaS/CRM.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
